methods.label: Add diameters and subtract overlaps
methods.explanation:
Adding the outside diameters would count some length twice at every link. We first determine that overlap.

Where two rings hang against each other, the inner bottom of the upper ring meets the inner top of the lower ring. The upper ring's outside bottom is \(1\) cm below this contact, and the lower ring's outside top is \(1\) cm above it. Their outside vertical spans therefore overlap by \(2\) cm. Consequently, each ring after the first adds its outside diameter minus \(2\) cm to the chain's length.

The outside diameters are \(20,19,\ldots,3\), so there are
\[
20-3+1=18
\]
rings and \(17\) links. Pairing diameters from opposite ends gives \(20+3=19+4=\cdots=23\). The \(18\) diameters form \(9\) such pairs, with total \(9\cdot23=207\) cm.

Subtracting the overlap once for each link gives
\[
207-17\cdot2=173\text{ cm}.
\]
The distance is \(173\) cm, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: The consecutive-diameter sum is derived by pairing endpoints. Only elementary length arithmetic and circle-diameter knowledge are needed.
